To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

- the antimicrobial susceptibility patterns of bacterial species associated with respiratory diseases in pigs and dairy cattle are stable over time and are not influenced by differences in animal population densities; - the prevalence of resistance against beta lactam antimicrobial agents in bacterial species associated with mastitis in dairy cows is significantly influenced by the geographical distribution of animal farming structures; - in federal Länder marked with large-scale livestock farming structures, the prevalence of resistance is significantly higher for cephalosprins than for penecillins
the antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of bacteria isolated from food-producing animals in Germany is not uniform.

the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria associated with respiratory diseases and mastitis in food-producing animals is low in Germany and that this is due to the implementation of appropriate measures to control infectious diseases in animals.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: - Monitoring of antimicrobial susceptibility in selected bacterial species associated with mastitis and respiratory diseases in food-producing animal species.
the development of a comprehensive strategy to control antimicrobial resistance.
the development of a monitoring system, apt to detect and evaluate the emergence of resistance against antimicrobial agents used in food-producing animals, in a continuous and representative manner.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results of this study indicate that, in Germany, the development of resistance to antimicrobial agents is currently not a major problem.

the data obtained in both studies are in agreement with the assumption that the implementation of preventive measures in the individual federal Länder is reflected in the occurrence of resistance against antimicrobial agents in the bacterial species examined.
the data collected in this representative, cross-sectional study on a national level do not support the thesis of a general increase of antimicrobial resistance in Germany.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the data obtained in the two studies are encouraging, but do not justify a complacent attitude.
, on a national basis, the prevalence of resistance is lower in Germany than in many other countries.

, despite the fact that a representative monitoring study on a nationwide scale was not conducted before, a considerable decrease in resistance rates could be measured in Germany in the course of the past decade.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a representative, crosssectional study is a useful tool to monitor the occurrence of resistance in bacteria associated with infectious disease patterns.

, by means of a comprehensive monitoring study, a representative and valid basis for the development of preventive strategies to control the development of resistance in bacterial populations is provided.
the implementation of preventive strategies in animal health services can effectively reduce the prevalence of resistance.
